standard.title: Explore needs and test materials
standard.description: explore needs or opportunities for designing, and test materials, components, tools, equipment and processes needed to create designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can generate and communicate design ideas through describing, drawing or modelling (AC9TDE2P01) and use materials, components, tools and equipment to safely make designed solutions (AC9TDE2P02). They have not yet explored needs systematically or tested materials for suitability before designing.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore needs or opportunities for designing, and test materials, components, tools, equipment and processes for suitability before creating designed solutions.

nodes.label: Identifying needs and design opportunities
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe a need or opportunity that could be addressed through a designed solution
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one need or opportunity and describe what kind of designed solution could address it
nodes.typical_width: Explore a range of needs and opportunities for designing (functional, community, environmental); describe what design opportunities each presents; examine existing products or services that address similar needs to inform design thinking
wider: Explore the designs and performance of models of First Nations Australians' watercraft — investigate the opportunity for their design principles to inform a new floating toy design
Examine local products and services (e.g. food distribution at a community event, school access features) and identify design opportunities for improvement, innovation or sustainability
success_criteria: Identifies a specific need or opportunity (not just 'I want to make something')
Describes what a designed solution would need to do to address it
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify a specific design need cannot conduct purposeful material testing in N2 — testing without a design purpose produces observations but not selection reasoning.

nodes.label: Testing materials for suitability
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can test materials under relevant conditions and describe what the test revealed about suitability for a design purpose
nodes.minimum_width: Test at least one material for a specific property relevant to a design purpose (e.g. strength, flexibility, compostability) and describe what the test revealed
nodes.typical_width: Test a range of materials under different conditions for suitability — including sustainability considerations (compostability, durability of natural materials); describe what each test reveals and use results to make material selection judgements
wider: Explore materials from a range of cultural contexts (e.g. shelters, boats, handmade tools, baskets from an Asian country) — test or compare equivalent materials and describe how their properties make them suited to different design applications

Test joining techniques (fabric, paper, cardboard) and evaluate which is strongest, most flexible or most appropriate for the design purpose — explain how the testing process informed the selection decision

response_modes.reason: Students often test only one property (e.g. strength) without considering that the relevant property depends on the design purpose. Testing across different material types and properties — including sustainability properties like compostability — builds a more complete understanding of what 'suitable' means.

success_criteria: Conducts a test on at least one material
Describes what the test revealed about the material's suitability for the design purpose
nodes.hinge_reason: Material test results are the primary input to N3 decisions about what is needed for the design solution — students who conduct no genuine testing arrive at N3 without evidence for their component and process choices.

nodes.label: Testing components, tools and processes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can test components, tools or processes and describe what testing reveals about which are needed for a designed solution
nodes.minimum_width: Test one tool, component or process and describe how the test informed a design decision
nodes.typical_width: Test a range of components, tools, equipment and processes for suitability; use test results alongside material testing to make decisions about what is needed to create the designed solution; document test findings
wider: Test and compare joining techniques (adhesives, stitching, fasteners) for a specific design purpose — evaluate which technique best balances strength, aesthetics and ease of use, and justify the choice
Explore how virtual reality or simulations can be used to test assembling processes before physical production — discuss what testing digitally reveals and what it does not

response_modes.reason: Testing components and processes alongside materials (node 2) into a coherent set of design decisions is the integration challenge. Students often treat material testing and tool/process testing as separate activities — this node asks them to use all test findings together to inform what the solution will need.

success_criteria: Tests at least one component, tool or process
Connects the test finding to a specific design decision
